guideSummary.surfnerd: Cannon Beach is a long, exposed beachbreak sitting south of Ocean Cape, breaking over sand with both lefts and rights on offer. It tends to be the last resort around here, the spot that still has something to ride when the rest of the ocean goes flat. The wave is easygoing and well suited to beginners.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Cannon Beach in Mainland is an exposed beach break that has inconsistent surf. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Offshore winds are from the northeast. Windswells and groundswells in equal measure and the best swell direction is from the west southwest. Waves at the beach break both left and right. The location means that it never gets crowded. Watch out for dangerous rips. Cannon Beach

guideSummary.surfnerd: Graveyard is a sand-bottom left point tucked inside the estuary at Yakutat, the best-known surf zone in Southeast Alaska and nicknamed "The Far North Shore". Swells wrap around Point Carrew and clean up along shifting sandbars before reaching the break, and since the sand is in constant flux the setup keeps changing. It favours lefts with real power and the occasional barrel, plus a short, steep right on smaller days.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Mill Bay is a town break in Kodiak City, with a reef in the middle of the beach that can hold sandbars, though the wave is pretty average. For something better, the headland off Spruce Cape holds more consistent rights. Much of Kodiak City sits in the swell shadow of Woody and Long Island, which do have spots along their north and east-facing coasts, and Fort Abercrombie State Historic Park hides Boneyard, a testing reefbreak.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Point Carrew is a left-hand point on an exposed outer headland, looking across Yakutat Bay toward the Malaspina Glacier and Mt St Elias. It picks up plenty of swell and throws it over sand and scattered boulder banks. Conditions are often messy and blown-out, and strong current sweeping out of the bay adds to the difficulty, so it suits confident surfers.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Sandy Beach sits on Baranof Island, part of the barrier that shelters Alaska's Inside Passage. Yakutat and Kodiak get more attention, but this is one of the most accessible places to paddle out in the region and the only Sitka break you can reach by road. It never gets truly world-class, yet its easy access and gentle nature make it a good place to learn.

guideSummary.surfForecast: Monashka Bay in Kodiak Island is a sheltered beach break that only works once in a while The best wind direction is from the southwest. Waves just as likely from local windswells as from distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the northeast. The beach break provides left and right handers. Even when there are waves, it's not likley to be crowded. Take care of the strong rips here. Monashka Bay
